criteria: `record.py` implements two functions: `parse_record(text, delimiter=",")`, which returns a `list[str]`, and `format_record(fields, delimiter=",")`, which returns a `str`.
`parse_record` splits fields on the delimiter. The empty string is one empty field, `[""]`. `"a,,b"` gives `["a", "", "b"]` and `"a,"` gives `["a", ""]`.

In `parse_record`, a field whose first character is `"` is a quoted field and runs to the closing quote. Inside it, two quotes `""` stand for one quote character, and the delimiter, `"\n"` and `"\r"` are ordinary characters.

In `parse_record`, the character right after a quoted field's closing quote must be the delimiter or the end of the text. Anything else raises `ValueError`, so `"a"b` (with the quotes) is invalid. A quoted field that never closes raises `ValueError`.

In `parse_record`, a field that does not start with `"` is an unquoted field. It is taken as it is with spaces kept, so `" a , b "` gives `[" a ", " b "]`. A `"` anywhere inside an unquoted field raises `ValueError`, so `ab"c` is invalid.
`parse_record` parses one record: `"\n"` or `"\r"` outside a quoted field raises `ValueError`.

`format_record` joins the fields with the delimiter. A field is written in quotes when it contains the delimiter, a `"`, `"\n"` or `"\r"`, or when it starts or ends with a space. Every other field, the empty string included, is written without quotes. Inside quotes, each `"` is doubled.
`format_record` raises `ValueError` unless `fields` holds at least one field and every field is a `str`.
For every valid `fields` and delimiter `d`, `parse_record(format_record(fields, d), d) == list(fields)`.
Both `parse_record` and `format_record` raise `ValueError` unless `delimiter` is exactly one character and is not `"`, `"\n"` or `"\r"`.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
